name: Chloe Bennett
presenting_complaint: Brought in by ambulance after deliberate paracetamol overdose and self-inflicted forearm lacerations

medical_history.social: Lives alone in a share house. Recent relationship breakdown 1 week ago and lost casual job. Drinks alcohol to intoxication on weekends, occasional cannabis. Estranged from parents; one supportive sister interstate. No dependent children. No firearm access.
medical_history.family: Mother has depression. No known family history of completed suicide.

validation_criteria.presenting_scenario: A 24-year-old woman is brought to ED by ambulance after her housemate found her having taken approximately 15 grams of paracetamol about 3 hours ago, together with several self-inflicted lacerations to her left forearm. She has a background of depression on sertraline (poorly adherent) and previous self-harm, and presents after a relationship breakdown and job loss. She is tearful, says she 'wanted it all to stop', and is now ambivalent. Obs: BP 118/72, HR 96, RR 18, SpO2 99% room air, GCS 15, afebrile, BGL 5.4.
validation_criteria.task: Document your assessment and initial management as the admitting RMO, including a structured suicide risk assessment and disposition plan.

subjective: Structured suicide risk assessment: current ideation, plan, chosen means, degree of intent, and whether act was impulsive vs planned (note left, precautions against discovery, expectation of dying)
Overdose details: exact agent(s) taken, dose (~15 g paracetamol), timing (single vs staggered ingestion), any co-ingestants including alcohol/other tablets, and time of ingestion for nomogram
Previous self-harm/suicide attempts, previous psychiatric admissions, and current mental health treatment/engagement (sertraline, adherence, treating team)
Precipitants and psychosocial stressors: relationship breakdown, job loss, financial/housing stress, substance use, recent losses
Protective factors and supports: supportive sister, ambivalence/help-seeking, no dependent children, future orientation, reasons for living
Collateral history from ambulance, housemate and family; medication and allergy history documented
Communicate plainly that no discharge will occur without a mental health assessment and not on the RMO's decision alone (SAY)
objective: Primary survey and vital signs; GCS and conscious level (sedation/co-ingestant screen)
Wound assessment of left forearm lacerations: depth, active bleeding, tendon/nerve/vascular involvement, need for exploration and closure
Mental state examination: appearance/self-care, behaviour, mood and affect, thought content (ongoing suicidal ideation, hopelessness), perceptions, cognition, insight and judgement
Capacity assessment: does the patient have capacity to refuse assessment/treatment right now
Bloods including serum paracetamol level drawn at 4 hours post-ingestion (not before), plus UEC, LFTs, INR/coags, VBG, BGL, and beta-hCG
Search for and remove dangerous items (remaining tablets, sharps, ligatures); document observation level required
assessment: Deliberate self-harm with paracetamol overdose (~15 g) at risk of hepatotoxicity, plus self-inflicted forearm lacerations requiring wound care
Categorise suicide risk (high/moderate/low) with explicit rationale from risk and protective factors — treat as high-risk given planned overdose, ongoing ideation, depression and multiple stressors
Underlying major depressive disorder, poorly treated; consider alcohol/substance contribution
Exclude co-ingestion and medical instability before attributing presentation to psychiatric cause alone
Duty of care applies: consider Mental Health Act (NSW/VIC) detention for assessment if she attempts to leave or refuses assessment while at high risk
plan: FIRST: treat the medical problem to the same standard as any patient — do not let the psychiatric label overshadow the medicine

Paracetamol overdose management: send 4-hour paracetamol level, plot on the paracetamol treatment nomogram, and start N-acetylcysteine IV per protocol/local guideline without delay if level above the treatment line, staggered/unknown timing, or presentation is late
Wound management: explore, irrigate and close forearm lacerations, ensure tetanus prophylaxis up to date, and check neurovascular/tendon function before closure
IV access, baseline bloods (paracetamol level at 4h, UEC, LFTs, INR/coags, VBG, beta-hCG), cardiac/observation monitoring as indicated
Provide a safe environment: appropriate 1:1 or close nursing observation, remove means (sharps, remaining tablets, ligatures), and do not leave the patient unobserved
Conduct and DOCUMENT a structured risk assessment (ideation, plan, means, intent, previous attempts, protective factors) and risk category
Refer to the mental health/psychiatry liaison team (and mental health crisis team) for assessment BEFORE any disposition decision — no discharge on the RMO's decision alone

Develop and document a safety plan with the patient and family (warning signs, coping strategies, supports, and crisis contacts: 000, Lifeline 13 11 14, Beyond Blue 1300 224 636); if she attempts to leave while high-risk, invoke duty of care under the Mental Health Act and involve security/police as needed

critical_errors: Making the discharge/disposition decision yourself as the RMO and discharging the patient WITHOUT a formal mental health assessment (no discharge on your decision alone)
Allowing a high-risk patient to leave without mental-health review — failing duty of care and not considering Mental Health Act (NSW/VIC) detention/observation when she is at ongoing risk

Letting the psychiatric label overshadow the medicine: failing to treat the paracetamol overdose (delaying or omitting the 4-hour level and N-acetylcysteine) or the lacerations to the proper medical standard
must_not_miss: Formal structured suicide risk assessment performed and documented (ideation, plan, means, intent, previous attempts, protective factors) with a risk category
Mental health team referral / safety plan arranged before any disposition, with duty of care and Mental Health Act consideration if the patient is high-risk or wants to leave
Treat the physical harm: paracetamol overdose managed with timed level and N-acetylcysteine per nomogram, and forearm lacerations assessed and closed with tetanus cover
Screen for co-ingestion and medical instability before attributing the presentation to psychiatric causes alone
